# GPU Program Specialization

> Charles Durham's source handoff for rapidly specializing mathematical programs
> on NVIDIA GPUs. MIT for owned code; third-party exceptions are documented.

## Read in this order
- [Overview and techniques](README.md)
- [Categorized project map and entry points](docs/PROJECTS.md)
- [Research coverage and status](docs/RESEARCH_COVERAGE.md)
- [Architecture and lineage](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Adaptation workflow and integration prompt](docs/ADAPTATION.md)
- [Performance evidence and limits](docs/BENCHMARKS.md)
- [Build requirements](docs/BUILDING.md)
- [What was validated](docs/VALIDATION.md)

## Keep the reading set small
Choose a task in the project map, then read that component's public interface,
one implementation path and its corresponding tests. Do not ingest the entire
repository: vendored Boost/SQLite, duplicate historical headers, old benchmark
reports and the large provenance manifest are not necessary starting context.
Use docs/RESEARCH_COVERAGE.md to distinguish integrated mechanisms, standalone
experiments and proposed applications. Read only the benchmark report relevant
to the performance claim you need to check.

## Primary interfaces
- [Secant](projects/secant/secant.h): row expressions and fused statistics.
- [Odezza](projects/odezza/core/odezza.h): rollout scoring and native LM.
- [PTX Inject](projects/mm-ptx/ptx_inject.h): annotated PTX replacement sites.
- [Stack PTX](projects/mm-ptx/stack_ptx.h): stack-program host compiler.
- [AST PTX](projects/mm-ptx/ast_ptx.h): postorder-program host compiler.
- [Function patching](projects/cubin-function-patch/cubin_function_patch.h).
- [Prepared requests](projects/odezza/frontend/odezza_request.h).

Secant-SR is an example consumer. Historical settings adapters are not the current
toggle API. PTX injection still invokes a PTX compiler; direct SASS specialization
has architecture-specific requirements. Do not claim universal speedups or a
supported public SaaS product from this repository.
